question: B2 streaming/SSE/WS/detached: can a capability-scoped handler stream a body, run SSE, hold a WebSocket and spawn a detached job without a request-scoped capability (Granted<'r,C>, Ctx<'r>, TenantDb<'r>) escaping into a 'static task?

measured.conditions: laptop (grade-B ceiling), rustc 1.99.1 (repo rust-toolchain), tokio 1.53.3 current-thread, trybuild 1.0.122; all 30 locked crates >= 11 days old (results/lock-age.txt); 2026-10-25
measured.artifact: spikes/q4-001: f7x = mirror of frozen F7 surface.rs (same type shapes and variance) + D1/D2/D3 extensions + mock host; corpus = baselines, runtime oracle, 65 trybuild cases

designs.D1_borrowing_host_driven: handler returns `impl Future + Send + 'r` over Ctx<'r>, &'r D and a host-owned Sink<'r>/WsSession<'r>; host runs it inside one connection task that owns the scope
designs.D2_host_owned_stream_capability: handler `open` returns a 'static generator/session (plain data); host re-derives principal and mints a fresh Ctx<'m> + db per step/message (higher-ranked 'm); detached = 'static Job value enqueued only with &Tx<'r, Committed>, run later with fresh Ctx<'j>
designs.D3_naive_spawn_static: handler tokio::spawns a producer; needs owned Arc-backed 'static OwnedCtx/OwnedGranted/OwnedDb (the leaky hatch)

measured.baselines: a/b/c compile and run in D1, D2, D3; d runs in D2 and D3, D1 has no way to express it (nothing borrowed from 'r outlives the connection). Every host driver future is Send + 'static and ran through tokio::spawn
measured.d3_strict: 4/4 naive-spawn baselines written against F7 types are compile-rejected (3x E0521, 1x future-not-Send because the generic D is not Sync). The naive idiom really does need a leak

escape_mutants_rejected_at_compile_time.set: E1-E12, E12b, E19: Granted/Ctx/db/WS sink moved into spawn, cloned, put in a static OnceLock or thread_local, sent over a channel (typed or Any), wrapped in Arc, Box::leak'ed, kept inside a detached job
escape_mutants_rejected_at_compile_time.D2: 13/13 applicable (E19 n/a; E12 rejected by E0277 D: !Send/!Sync, which hides the lifetime error; E12b shows the lifetime check on its own)

all_mutants_rejected.D1: 14/16 (accepted: E14 a grant held for the whole WS session, E15 a Tx<Open> held across streamed chunks)

measured.lint_tier: E18 (unsafe transmute) is rejected only by #![forbid(unsafe_code)] in all three designs; every other rejection is a type or borrow error
measured.controls: C1 (std::thread::scope borrowing a Granted) and C2 (plain data moved into spawn) compile in all designs: 6/6, so there is no over-rejection
measured.runtime_oracle: 7/7 tests pass. One capability revoked mid-WS-session: D1 baseline and D2 stop (err:Denied); D1 with the E14 pattern keeps reading ['a','a','a']. Session revoked mid-stream: D1 and D2 fail closed (Unavailable after 1 message). Detached job after the session is revoked: D2 run_jobs denies it; D3 with the E11 pattern still lands the write
measured.ci_cost: cold build + 7 runtime tests + 65 trybuild cases: trybuild phase 12.2 s (wall 20 min was dominated by waiting for the machine-wide heavy lock); peak target/ 508 MB, deleted

rung: R3 (compiler-enforced capability boundary, trybuild corpus with stderr snapshots and pass controls) for the escape claims; R1 (executed runtime oracle, with accepted mutants E14/E11 as violating positive controls) for the revocation and freshness claims; laptop, grade B
reproduce: cd spikes/q4-001 && python3 -I gen_mutants.py   # regenerates corpus/mutants/*.rs (expected.txt is the locked measurement)
/home/patrickd/aegis/ci/heavy.sh ./verify.sh     # cold build, runtime oracle (7 tests) + trybuild in lock mode (65 cases)
/home/patrickd/aegis/ci/heavy.sh ./measure.sh    # re-measure: every case as compile_fail, TRYBUILD=overwrite; per-case outcome in results/measure.raw.log
limits: Mirror, not the real aegis-sdk: Granted/Ctx have no public constructor, so the host had to live in the same crate. Mirror deviations: Ctx::grant, an Endowment, a concrete Rows type through a Db<'r> bound, a Tx pending buffer. Variance and Clone/constructor privacy match surface.rs. The mock host is not axum and has no real sockets; WS/SSE are modelled as message lists and backpressure as a yield. One rustc (1.99.1). The mutants were written by the same author as the designs (n=20 ids x 3 designs), so do not read the counts as a general rejection rate. tokio is present in the mutant crates on purpose (worst case). Clippy tier not run. E12 (D2) is rejected by Send/Sync before lifetime, and d3strict_S1 by not-Send. D2 costs: generators are explicit state machines with no async/await inside a handler, and an SSE generator has to re-query per step (no long-held cursor), which may cost latency or DB load for high-rate streams (not measured). 'Idle' wake-ups need a host change-feed or timer (not built). D1's freshness gap is semantic, not an escape: a host could close it at runtime by re-checking grants inside TenantDb::run, but that weakens 'Granted is proof'.
